newsitem.title: UK: Weather dominates world grains crop outlook.
newsitem.headline: Weather dominates world grains crop outlook.

text.p: This year's extreme weather has created problems for grain farmers in many parts of the world.
Too much rain in some places and too little in others forced the International Grains Council, an authoritative monitor of the world's cereals market, to cut estimates for some countries' output.
But improvements elsewhere mean that world cereals production, seen at 1,481 million tonnes in the IGC's latest estimate, was only just below last year's bumper 1,484 million tonne crop.
Hot and dry weather in the corn belt led the IGC to cut its ideas on US maize output, by four million tonnes to 246 million, but still 10 million higher than last year's harvest.

A lower US maize crop is largely responsible for a cut in estimated world production of coarse grains (mainly maize, but also barley, sorghum, oats and rye) to 896 million, from 901 million estimated before and 902 million produced last year.

But optimism on the US wheat crop boosted ideas on world wheat production. Yields proved better than earlier forecasts, with early frost having had less of a negative impact than first thought, analysts said.
World wheat output this year was now put at 585 million tonnes compared with a previous estimate of 579 million and last year's crop of 582 million.
Central and Eastern European wheat crops will be lower than expected, largely because of rain this summer which has caused widespread flooding in the region.

But again, although the estimated total wheat crop for the region was cut to 32.4 million tonnes from 33.9, it is still well up on last year's 26.3 million tonnes. And the impact of the rain has been less than widely feared, according to IGC figures.
The El Nino weather pattern created worries in Australia about the new crop, although the IGC did not change its estimate, and concerns over excessive moisture in parts of South America.
"Wheat planting in Argentina has been delayed by wet weather in most regions of the grains belt near Buenos Aires," the IGC said in its monthly Grains Market Report.
Its forecast for Argentina's wheat crop was unchanged at 13.5 million tonnes.

Algerian production was hit by severe drought affecting two-thirds of the country, the IGC said, cutting its wheat production estimate to one million tonnes from an earlier forecast of 1.6 million and well under last year's 2.4 million tonnes.

As the greater part of the Algerian crop is durum wheat, the drought is one of the main factors behind an expected five million tonnes fall in the world durum crop this year to below 29 million tonnes. Lower output in the EU and a cut of almost one-third in the US durum crop were also factors, the IGC said.
